title: Who Gets Flagged? The Pluralistic Evaluation Gap in AI Content Watermarking

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing existing literature to identify disparities in watermark detection rates between native and non-native speakers, highlighting tokenization inefficiencies for non-Latin scripts, and proposing cross-lingual detection parity testing.

Analyzing the Western-centric skew of current evaluation datasets (e.g., ImageNet distributions) and proposing watermark evaluation across culturally diverse content, including non-Western visual traditions and diverse acoustic environments.

Highlighting existing benchmark findings (e.g., AudioMarkBench) that demonstrate differing watermark false positive rates based on biological sex, and advocating for mandatory demographic disaggregation of detection metrics.

Reviewing findings from audio watermarking benchmarks that stratify detection performance by age groups to reveal systematic disparities, proposing this demographic disaggregation as a standard evaluation requirement.
